items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Of course, Milt Galber was more pleased than he expected, and that was the beginning, as I say, the long series of albums.

ctx.x: To sum it up better, that was the begining of a beautiful thing --' recording wise and friendship wise, and a series of albums, running between 20 and 30. We made in the middle twenties, amoung of albums.

We got to the first date at Decca on 57th Street, and did our first album, and they're talking about mutual admiration societies -- ank and Haggard -- Haggard did some arrangements first, I can't remember what was on the first date, but of course that's another research project. We did so many albums. On that first date, there was "Jump for Joy" and "Kisses and Jubilation", and the playbacks were just way beyond what we expected. Of course, Milt Galber was more pleased than he expected, and that was the…

Now, as we progress with the albums, Haggard wished to increase the personnel on the records for some of the arrangements that he was doing. They wanted us to -- I've been associated with Bob Haggard and Yank Lawson, and the Lawson-Haggard Band. Since then, and those were the early boys, up until now -- up until the present time. Up until the last few years, I've been doing concerts -- they've done concerts all over the world, and I've done a great deal of them with them. Once in awhile, I would be busy on other…
